The Environment parameter map is initialized before constructing the actual Environment, and partial-initialization flags guard teardown. The stable heap Fixture owns the marker used by onRead. The outer callback scope deliberately selects nested depth with skipped task queues; it does not provide an unimplemented production checkpoint.

Controls inspect the actual provider, stream identity, wrapper brand and weak BindingData slot. The CloseReq Global test drops JS roots while completion retains the handle; after completion it observes weak-slot clearing without dereferencing the collected handle. GC tickets are checked as scalar captures after actual synchronous close, including the retained service after worker join. semantic_findings.finding: selectedHookException requires an actual current JS exception, extracts it through JS_GetException, compares identity against the selected expected reason, excludes uncatchable completion, and rethrows that same value. The installed guest hook actually throws. Unexpected reasons remain actual throws and cause a fixture error. This is explicitly selected test policy; it does not implement or qualify Node IsStackOverflowError, ReportFatalException, Environment::Exit(7), or uncaught fatal bootstrap.

Pinned Node FSReqPromise Reject/Resolve set finished, construct HandleScope and the void InternalCallbackScope, then perform the live promise property Get. The successor captures the real ordinary before-hook completion in the existing operation scope and continues only after initialization and async-ID push, for JavaScriptException and a nonfatal boundary. The subsequent live Get, actual JS_PiSettlePromise, native FromJust check, finished flag, callback-scope destruction, and cleanup retain their original order.

The actual Scope/Boundary owners distinguish retained earlier ordinary completion from a new current JS exception. Escaping captures the earlier reason before the live Get; later pending checks only stop for actual newly surfaced completion, while fatal/termination remains higher priority. The callback scope closes before the operation scope rethrows the retained reason. JS_PiSettlePromise still rejects an actually current pending exception and requires a genuine Promise, so no resolver stub or cached replacement was introduced.

The success and EBADF tests call the actual private FS read binding and retain real UV storage through completion. They distinguish the hook reason from a fulfilled or rejected Promise. The replacement-Promise test installs a real live property getter after request creation, requires the before hook to have run, and checks settlement of that returned Promise while the original stays pending. The getter and thrown reasons are actual guest operations.

The fixture acquires the actual native queue through acquireNative with explicit hook identity; the owner refuses a conflicting hook set. Real queue dispatch captures completion before ticket destruction and delegates caught completion only after that destruction. The fixture policy is bounded observation of this path and does not masquerade as the production uncaught-exception policy.

The fixture supplies an actual present-object FileHandle internal class/prototype and invokes the concrete constructor owner. A dedicated control requires the complete public FileHandle callback template to remain explicitly unavailable. The packet does not silently substitute a complete StreamBase method table or public fs bootstrap.
